name: Summoner
description:
That's a big dragon. It could smash you under its foot without even noticing. Good thing you're not the one who'll be fighting it. Your hand flits thoughtfully over the glass flasks at your hip. Who's the right pick for this? Not Tesoro - he's not ready for a fight this big. Not Pulce - he's big enough, but he's still recovering from that nasty fall yesterday. Patatina? Yes, Patatina. Everyone always underestimates Patatina. Yes, perfect. You pull the flask from its holster and hold it up, taking in its pale glow. You hope the training has been enough. This will be her biggest test yet. You loosen the cap and, with a shout, cast its contents into the air before you. The glowing liquid expands into a mist, which twists and condenses before you, forming first a pair of wide, flat, furry feet, then a pair of stout legs, then a broad, armored trunk, two scaly arms with sticky claws at their ends, and finally the fuzzy head, snub nose and beady eyes you've come to know and love. Twelve feet tall, Patatina looks lovingly back at you, then turns to the foe before her. Her single, thick eyebrow furrows, her wide red mouth bares its needle-sharp teeth, and with a deep bellow, Patatina charges toward the dragon, fearless.

While other adventurers are limited to cultivating their own capabilities, Summoners have access to an entire world of creatures, which they capture and train to fight for them. They hold these creatures in special magical vessels, which they craft themselves, calling each creature forth as needed and taking time between battles to train and even befriend the creatures they keep.

The Summoner mestiere is entirely focused on capturing and training creatures you encounter on your adventures, and bringing them into battle. You will craft your own vessels from mundane objects you choose, use the Capture ability to capture creatures, and with the Keeper of Vessels ability, you'll carry a subset of active vessels with you, using the Summon ability to bring a creature out of its vessel and onto the battlefield. A summoned creature fights in your stead - commanding its movements and actions requires your full attention - and you have full access to and control over its character sheet.

Between battles, you can use your Train ability to help your captured creatures become stronger, learn new abilities, and increase the bond of Friendship between you (as defined by the Friendship ability). You yourself have some very basic combat training which you can use to defend yourself in a pinch, but by and large you will remain on the sidelines as your summoned beasts do the fighting for you.

Summoner offers a huge variety of options - as wide as the menagerie you manage to capture.

Play a Summoner if you want to:

  • Build and tend a roster of unique creatures, investing in their growth over time and managing a collection that grows stronger as your adventures range farther and wider.

  • Fight with friendship, winning creatures over through presence, empathy, or negotiation, and growing those bonds into something genuinely powerful.

  • Be the monster, controlling the actions of the creatures you summon in battle, exploring a massive variety of abilities.

Questions to consider when making a Summoner:

  • What drew them to this practice? The crafting of vessels, the thrill of capture, the appeal of companionship, or an older tradition they were born into?

  • How do they feel about the creatures in their care? Are the vessels a kind of kindness—giving wild beings safety and purpose—or do they have reservations or guilt about the nature of what they do?

  • Which of their starting captured creatures has the deepest Friendship, and what did it take to get there? What has tested that bond? What has strengthened it?

  • What kind of vessels do they make? The choice of object and components is personal—is there a pattern to their choices, a material they favor, a form that means something to them?

  • Is there a creature they have tried and failed to capture? One they are still looking for?

novizio.description: You are trained in the art of crafting vessels, as well as capturing and summoning creatures. You have a humble collection of vessels and creatures.
novizio.baseMpNotes: Summoner abilities to not have an MP cost. The creatures you summon may have their own base MP.
novizio.abilities:
Capture, Craft Vessel, Friendship, Keeper of Vessels, Summon, Train.

When you gain these abilities, craft any number of vessels costing no more than 5 treasure total. Then choose any number of creatures native to the biome of one of your home cultures with a combined Challenge of 10 or less, and place each creature in one of your vessels.
novizio.gratuiti: A belt, bag, harness or bandolier for your vessels. A chew toy, a small bag of treats.
